assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model's electroweak sector and is one of the clearest, most consequential measurements in modern physics. It required general-purpose detectors of unprecedented scale and a decisive, independent two-experiment confirmation.
assessment.attribution: The detectors were conceived and led by long-term founders of the ATLAS and CMS collaborations; Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are the natural founding-spokesperson trio. Gianotti led ATLAS at announcement time and is a serious alternative, so the choice among four names is contestable. Any prize must credit instrument leadership while acknowledging that thousands of collaborators made the result.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by two experiments, with a decade of coupling and spin-parity measurements consistent with the Standard Model. The 2013 prize recognised the theory; experimental recognition is mature and, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Fairness of limiting a collaboration discovery to three people, and which leadership roles are decisive.
Overlap with candidate B026 on the detectors; this ballot treats the discovery rather than machine construction as the core.
I rely on my own knowledge of the collaborations' histories and have not verified spokesperson dates independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy by detecting a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and by associating neutrinos with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane. It is a genuine new window on the Universe, realised by a very large instrumented-ice detector.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and its predecessor AMANDA; Spiering was a leading figure in the field's early detector development and in establishing the collaboration. A two-person credit is plausible, but a prize might need to consider other pioneers of the high-energy neutrino programme, such as the DUMAND and Baikal efforts, not named here.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established and the instrument is mature. Source identification is still a small number of associations; KM3NeT and further IceCube analyses should sharpen the picture, so the field is established while source astrophysics is still developing.
uncertainties: Strength of individual source associations beyond TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane is still evolving.
Attribution among early pioneers of large neutrino telescopes is not fully captured by two names.
I have not independently verified significance levels quoted in the literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-angle prediction of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity opened the entire field of moire quantum materials, with strong originality and a broad spread of follow-up work.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the experimental discovery. This theory-plus-experiment pairing gives a clean three-person configuration, though other groups, notably those who developed twist control and later correlated-state work, also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups, and the platform has led to many further phenomena, but the microscopic origin of the superconductivity remains debated and the field is still young, so timing may be early for some.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and the interpretation of the correlated phases remain unsettled.
Sample variability and twist-angle disorder complicate reproducibility.
Whether a prize now is premature relative to a more settled picture.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reaching 10^-18 fractional uncertainty transformed time-keeping and enable tests of relativity, searches for varying constants and relativistic geodesy. The magic-wavelength idea together with the demonstrations of extreme precision are conceptually clear and technically impressive.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept; Ye's group demonstrated the lowest systematic uncertainties and many applications. This is a compact and fair two-person credit, with the caveat that ion-clock and other lattice-clock groups also advanced the field.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in several laboratories, and the redefinition of the SI second is under discussion, which suggests the technology is mature and recognition would be timely. Optical frequency combs were already recognised in 2005.
uncertainties: Overlap in spirit with the 2005 frequency-comb prize.
Contributions of other clock groups, for example Al+ ion clocks and Sr-lattice groups elsewhere, may deserve consideration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Event Horizon Telescope delivered the first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A*, a milestone of instrumentation and data analysis and direct visual evidence for black-hole shadows. It is a remarkable technical achievement in VLBI at 1.3 mm.
assessment.attribution: Doeleman led the project and the VLBI development; Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept and led the science case; Moran contributed decisively to the array and to mm-VLBI. This is a plausible trio, but a collaboration of hundreds makes any credit contestable.
assessment.maturity: Two sources imaged, with consistent shadow sizes, but interpretation, such as spin and jet launching, rests on simulations and ongoing polarisation work. The black-hole prizes of 2020 already recognised the objects, so the incremental scientific novelty is more modest.
uncertainties: Relative novelty after the 2020 prize for black holes.
Which individuals were decisive in a very large collaboration.
Model-dependent interpretation of the images.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, from the Mott-insulator transition to controllable many-body Hamiltonians, created a new experimental platform for strongly correlated matter and has had a broad influence on condensed-matter physics and quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Cirac supplied the theoretical proposals, including the Bose-Hubbard realisation by Jaksch and others, while Bloch built the leading experimental programme; Greiner and Esslinger also made decisive experiments. Choosing three out of five is difficult, and Jaksch is not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with many independent groups and quantum-gas microscopy, although the scientific payoff for open problems such as the Fermi-Hubbard phase diagram is still developing. BEC and laser cooling already received earlier recognition.
uncertainties: Selection among five credited names is contestable and the key theory paper's first author is missing from the list.
Overlap with earlier Nobel recognition of cold-atom methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon microstrip and pixel detectors made precision vertexing and tracking routine at modern colliders, enabling heavy-flavour tagging and the Higgs and top programmes, and have spread into imaging and space instruments. As an experimentalist I regard the impact as extremely large and the invention as clear.
assessment.attribution: Kemmer pioneered planar processing for detectors, Parker developed the microstrip detector and Heijne the pixel hybrid approach. This three-person configuration is broadly sensible, though other groups, such as the hybrid pixel and the monolithic detector developers, are also relevant.
assessment.maturity: Mature and universally adopted in particle physics, space instrumentation and photon science. Recognition would be late rather than premature. I note my own field proximity as a potential bias and I weigh the candidate on the supplied evidence.
uncertainties: Instrumentation recognition has precedent but is infrequent, and the contribution may be viewed as technology rather than discovery.
Attribution among several parallel developments is uncertain.
My professional proximity to detector work may incline me favourably.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, established a new class of quantum matter with robust edge and surface states and had a wide influence on condensed-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the foundational theory, while Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realisation; Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's HgTe proposal is not in the credited list and complicates an equitable configuration.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by multiple experiments, with sustained activity, though much of the practical promise has not materialised and the 2016 prize recognised topological phase transitions and phases of matter more broadly.
uncertainties: Missing theory credit for the HgTe prediction among the supplied names.
Overlap with the topological theme of the 2016 prize.
